# ChatGPT audit of Rome, Solved. (86 pp) — pasted by the owner, 2026-10-26 (French)

Scores: visual identity 9, art direction 9, structure 8.5, writing 8, practical use 8, factual precision 6, reader fit 7, commercial 8, ready 6.5.

Key points (summarised faithfully from the owner's paste):
1. Marks (Established/Official/Surveyed/Volatile) don't let a reader find the source: add compact references (body, page title, date checked, link/QR) for important claims.
2. The "1.5 km radius around Piazza Venezia" image: define it precisely (as-the-crow-flies vs walking distance vs walking time; what lies outside).
3. D01: the Centro Storico/Monti vs Termini opposition is too strong; make the exceptions (train-heavy trips, budget, many day trips) visible in the initial recommendation; give the start points of walking times.
4. D02 (priority high): Tap & Go — ATAC applies the best fare per 24 h: after more than four BIT, the sixth purchase triggers the Roma 24H fare (€8.50), valid 24 h from the first tap; Tap & Go is individual — one card cannot pay for several travelers. The book must say the conditions, one card per traveler, and to re-check before travel.
5. D03: €55 Fiumicino ↔ inside the Aurelian Walls matches the municipal tariff; add the official reference and date near the fare; distinguish fixed fare / other destinations / supplements / onward hop; depends on party size and bags.
6. D04: half-day for the ancient core presented as default — give two variants (essential half-day; deeper full day).
7. D05: two lines (ticket vs security) is excellent; soften absolute wording — paid services differ.
8. Bookings (pp. 35–38): windows change; add an operational table: sight · action · when to check · official source — directing to updated rules rather than freezing windows.
9. Money/tipping: distinguish regulation vs common practice vs the book's advice. Coperto (priority very high): the claim that coperto is banned in Lazio must be backed by the exact legal provision and its current status, or softened.
10. Ostia/closures/strikes/entry formalities: date-dependent; EES/ETIAS/passport must be checked on official EU sources with a date, and stated as rules for US citizens, not universal.
11. Pp. 52–75: durations as estimates; distinguish traveler profiles; the 90-second rule as a heuristic, not infallible.
12. Pp. 76–86: the pocket card (wallet card) must be at least as rigorous as the text; categorical shortcuts (passes, coperto, bookings) must be precise there too; add a discreet pointer to the updated sheet.
Top five: coperto legal basis; Tap & Go explanation; audit all prices/hours/windows; formalities by nationality; sources + date checked.
Production: phone readability, links, Field Sheet availability, pocket card vs text concordance.
